item.title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776” — Sun Sep 20, 7:00 PM — NJ
item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.title: NJ Death Cafe — Mon Sep 21, 7:00 PM — Freeman Gardens
item.description:
We invite you to join us for a Death Cafe. A Death Cafe is a welcoming, facilitated discussion space where people come together to talk openly and honestly about life, death, and dying—over tea, cake, refreshments, and meaningful conversation. It’s an opportunity to reflect on, explore, and share personal thoughts, emerging ideas, and lived experiences. Participants are invited to listen to and engage with others in a safe, confidential, and nonjudgmental environment while contemplating mortality. Ultimately, by talking about death, we create space to live more fully—with greater intention, presence, and purpose. All are welcome! Contact us at njdeathcafe@gmail.com Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook

item.description: Community drum and chant circle rooted in Sufi prayer. Meets every other Monday: September 28, October 12, etc. Contribution: Sliding scale donation $20–$40 (no one will be turned away) This is a vibrant Community Drum and Chanting Circle, where we drum and chant from our hearts into the universe. This experience is open to absolutely everyone, regardless of background or belief system—all that’s required is an open heart and a willingness to connect through sound. The term ‘lover’ in this context refers to seekers on the Sufi path who are longing for union with the divine energy. You can think of this gathering as an expansion of the sema sufi meditations we used to offer. It is looser in form, more focused on music, and does not necessarily involve whirling, although it is welcome if you are called to it. There is a rhythm older than thought. item.title: Tuesday Night Figure Drawing - Open Studio — Tue Sep 29, 8:00 AM — the Space
item.description:
Tuesday Night Figure Drawing – Open Studio *Cover art by Ling Chen.
Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Wed Sep 30, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.title: Nutrition Trends + Myths — Wed Sep 30, 2:00 PM — University Hall 2009 - Classroom
item.description:
Have you ever seen a TikTok about a new diet, food, or recipe that someone claimed "fixed all their problems?" You're not the only one! Non-nutrition professionals in media love to talk about nutrition like they're experts, but do you know how to identify the professionals from the influencers? Come to this MSDO meeting to explore current nutrition trends circulating the media, learn how to critically analyze information you view, and maybe even engage in some interesting conversations about your own nutrition beliefs. This space is welcome to all, and this includes different belief systems around food. This will not be a space to shame, guilt, or tell you if what you're eating is right or wrong. We encourage everyone to come with an open-mind and the curiosity to know more!
Hosted by: Dietetics Organization
Online Location: https://montclair.zoom.us/j/91867896766

item.title: Mindful Masculinity: A Circle of Brotherhood — Wed Sep 30, 7:00 PM — the Space
item.description:
We Meet Bi-Weekly, Every Other Wednesday · 7:00 – 8:30 PM · $15 Through open dialogue, mindfulness, and other calming practices, we quiet the mind, open the heart, and deepen our connection to ourselves and each other. The circle is open to all male identifying individuals. Meetings are hosted by Leo A. Sante – mindfulness coach, teacher, and dad. We start by sharing our wins and challenges, honoring each voice without judgment or advice. From there, we move into practices that help us release stress, shift perspective, and bring awareness and resilience into our lives. Each week centers on a different theme to help guide us – trust, accomplishment, family, rest, intimacy, presence – as we discover new ways to move through the world as mindful men. Come as you are. Leave more grounded, connected, and inspired. Connect with Leo: Instagram: @holdingpresence Online: HoldingPresence.com Email: pe***********@***il.com
Source: The Space For Art

item.title: Tea & Tarot - A bookclub style discussion group — Thu Oct 15, 7:00 PM — the Space
item.description:
Monthly Gathering | Thursday, October 15th | 7:00 PM – 8:30 PM | The Space | $25 Calling all tarot lovers, both new and seasoned! Join us for an intimate way of exploring the cards. What could be better than a cozy evening of warm tea and deep conversation? Join us for Tea & Tarot with Gina Devine—a monthly, book club-style discussion group created to deepen our connection with the archetypes of the tarot through community and shared insight. Rather than a formal class, this is a casual meet-up where we treat the tarot as a living text. Based on the psychological insights of Carl Jung, we will explore the Major Arcana not just as fortune-telling tools, but as mirrors of our own lives, rituals, and transformations. The Experience Each month, we open a new gateway of creative and spiritual exploration. Our time together includes:
Archetypal Deep Dives: We’ll focus on a specific theme or set of cards each session, discussing their symbolism and how they show up in our modern world
